assessment.nobel_worthiness: Unifying electron dynamics and ionic motion in a single fictitious-Lagrangian scheme made first-principles molecular dynamics practical and opened finite-temperature, bonding-changing simulation of liquids, amorphous solids, surfaces and chemical reactions from DFT. Original, clear, and transformative for computational materials science and chemistry; it is the methodological backbone of much modern electronic-structure work.
assessment.attribution: The 1985 paper is by Car and Parrinello alone, so the two-name configuration is natural and the credit is unusually clean. Later extensions (Born-Oppenheimer AIMD, Parrinello-Rahman-type work) are separate and need not be rewarded here.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of use, thousands of independent implementations and applications; recognition is long overdue rather than premature. Its fit to the physics prize rather than chemistry is a judgement call but defensible given the condensed-matter foundations.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views the method as physics or chemistry/computational science.
Parrinello's other contributions (metadynamics, etc.) could blur what the prize cites.
Fine details of priority and historical context are from my own recollection and not verified here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall state and Z2 classification, followed by its experimental realization in HgTe quantum wells, created the field of topological insulators and a new organizing principle for band structures. Deep conceptual originality, with clear lasting impact across condensed matter, materials theory and spintronics, and strong ties to first-principles materials prediction.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical papers (graphene QSH, Z2 invariant); Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang's HgTe proposal and Molenkamp's group's 2007 experiment complete the story. The three-name triple is credible, but Zhang's untimely death and the competing 3D TI work (Moore-Balents, Fu-Kane, Hasan, Cava) leave allocation contentious.
assessment.maturity: Experimental confirmation is extensive and independent (HgTe, 3D Bi-based TIs, ARPES, transport); interpretation is stable. Timing is arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Credit among Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, Fu, Moore, Balents, Hasan and others is unresolved and not all those people are on this entry's credited list.
Zhang's absence constrains a fair configuration.
Quantum anomalous Hall realization is a separate part that may need different recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2008 discovery of superconductivity in iron pnictides opened a second family of high-Tc superconductors with a new interplay of magnetism, orbital physics and multiband Fermi surfaces. It is a major, clearly identifiable materials discovery, with extensive follow-up in electronic-structure theory, spin fluctuations and pairing symmetry.
assessment.attribution: Hosono's group reported LaFeAsO(F) at ~26 K, the decisive discovery; rapid Tc increases to ~55 K in Sm-based compounds came from Chen and Zhao's groups. A Hosono plus one Chinese-group configuration is plausible, but Chen's contribution is also strong and picking between them is delicate.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently and quickly worldwide; maturity is high after nearly two decades. The pairing mechanism remains unsettled, but the discovery itself is secure, much as in the 1987 cuprate case.
uncertainties: The microscopic pairing mechanism is still unresolved, which might lead some members to feel the field is not complete.
Choice between Chen and Zhao for the Chinese-group credit is a judgement call.
Recollection of Tc values and priority is from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model predicted flat bands at magic angles in twisted bilayer graphene, and the experimental observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity gave a tunable platform for strongly correlated physics. Creative, with a rare theory-prediction/experiment pairing that has spawned moire quantum matter as a field, including fractional Chern insulators.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald's theory and Jarillo-Herrero's group's experiments (with Yuan Cao as lead author, not credited on the list) are the most coherent trio; others such as Dean, Kim, Santos and Lopes dos Santos also made early contributions.
assessment.maturity: Roughly eight years since 2018 experiments, with many independent replications, but the interpretation of the superconducting state and the correlated phases is still evolving. Recognition is plausible but somewhat early relative to the longest-standing candidates.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism and nature of correlated states remain debated.
Reproducibility across devices and sample-dependent behavior.
Early-career contributors not on the credited list limit attribution fairness.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Realizing Hubbard-model physics, the superfluid to Mott-insulator transition, and fermionic many-body states with cold atoms in optical lattices built a quantum simulator with direct relevance to correlated-electron models I work on. Great conceptual clarity and lasting impact, though much of its promise is as a simulator rather than a source of new answers for real materials.
assessment.attribution: Zoller's theoretical proposal (Jaksch et al.) enabled the experiments; Greiner-Bloch observed the Mott transition; Esslinger realized fermionic Mott and related states. With four credited names, the allocation to three is awkward whichever is omitted.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of consistent confirmation by many groups, with mature techniques (quantum gas microscopes). Timing is reasonable, though more definitive results beyond classical simulation may emerge.
uncertainties: Choice among four credited people is difficult and cannot be settled by the supplied information.
Overlap with the Cirac-Zoller candidates and other quantum-simulation candidates may split recognition.
The significance for materials physics versus proof of principle is debatable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2012 observation of the Higgs boson completed the Standard Model's particle content and is among the most important experimental results in modern physics. Clarity and impact are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: The 2013 prize recognized the theory, leaving the experiment open, but the discovery is the product of thousands of physicists, and the prize rules constrain recognition to three. The ATLAS and CMS spokespersons and project initiators (Jenni, Della Negra, Virdee, Gianotti) are the typical choices, and Evans for the LHC is a separate machine contribution. Any three is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed by two experiments and subsequent coupling measurements; mature. Because of the 2013 award, the argument for a second prize is mainly about collaboration credit.
uncertainties: Fairness of recognizing individuals for collaboration work is controversial.
Whether the Committee sees the experimental discovery as already honored in 2013.
Choice of three from five credited people is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock concept (magic wavelength trapping) and its realization at 10^-18 precision revolutionized time measurement, with prospects in tests of fundamental physics, geodesy and a redefinition of the second.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice clock and Ye brought it to extreme precision and many-body clocks; a two-name award is clean, though Hall and Hansch were already honored for combs which Ye used.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs have reached comparable accuracy; the SI redefinition is still pending, so timing could be either slightly early or well-judged.
uncertainties: Whether to wait for a redefinition of the second.
Other groups (e.g., Ludlow, Bloom, Lemke, Schmidt, Lisdat) also contributed to performance records.
I assess this outside my own field, so my confidence is lower.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The spin Hall effect, its prediction and observation in semiconductors and metals, underpins charge-to-spin conversion for spin-orbit torque and modern spintronics, which is close to my area of magnetization dynamics. Scientifically clear, with growing technological relevance.
assessment.attribution: Dyakonov and Perel made the original 1971 prediction; Hirsch's 1999 re-proposal, and Kato-Awschalom and Wunderlich-Jungwirth in 2004-05 are the key observations. Attribution is intricate, and Hirsch, Zhang, Sinova and Murakami, Nagaosa and Zhang (intrinsic SHE) are absent from the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced widely in metals and semiconductors, and used in devices. The decisive-credit puzzle and the possibility that a prize would be better framed around spintronics more broadly weigh against urgency.
uncertainties: Priority and the roles of intrinsic versus extrinsic mechanisms are tangled.
Competing spintronics candidates (GMR was recognized in 2007) may reduce the case.
Details of the experimental chronology are from memory.
